antidotes.why: Forgiveness cures anger by setting patience against reactive anger only, never against the wronged first.
Put out anger with good sense as fire with water; do not decide when angry.
Steadiness makes whoever can withstand the surge of desire and anger here happy.
Words that do not wound; answer fire with water.
Free of clinging, fear and anger: the steady one.

chains.summary: Arjuna asks what pushes a person to do wrong against their own wish. Krishna says it is desire and anger born of rajas, and this covers knowing as smoke covers fire and dust covers a mirror.
chains.title: What drives us against our will

verses.m: Arjuna said: Then what drives a person to do wrong, Krishna, even against his will, as if pushed by force?
verses.sa: अर्जुन उवाचअथ केन प्रयुक्तोऽयं पापं चरति पूरुषः । अनिच्छन्नपि वार्ष्णेय बलादिव नियोजितः ॥

verses.m: The Blessed Lord said: It is desire, it is anger, born of the quality of passion; all-devouring and greatly harmful. Know this to be the enemy here.
verses.sa: श्री भगवानुवाचकाम एष क्रोध एष रजोगुणसमुद्भवः । महाशनो महापाप्मा विद्ध्येनमिह वैरिणम् ॥

verses.m: As fire is covered by smoke, a mirror by dust, and an embryo by the womb, so is this wisdom covered by desire.
verses.sa: धूमेनाव्रियते वह्निर्यथाऽऽदर्शो मलेन च । यथोल्बेनावृतो गर्भस्तथा तेनेदमावृतम् ॥

chains.summary: Dwelling on an object breeds attachment. Attachment breeds desire. Desire breeds anger. Anger breeds delusion. Delusion causes loss of memory. Loss of memory ruins judgement. With judgement gone, one is lost.
chains.title: The ladder of fall

verses.m: When a person dwells on objects, attachment to them is born. From attachment comes desire, and from desire, anger.
verses.sa: ध्यायतो विषयान्पुंसः सङ्गस्तेषूपजायते । सङ्गात् संजायते कामः कामात्क्रोधोऽभिजायते ॥

verses.m: From anger comes delusion; from delusion, confusion of memory; from confusion of memory, the ruin of understanding; and with understanding ruined, a person is lost.
verses.sa: क्रोधाद्भवति संमोहः संमोहात्स्मृतिविभ्रमः । स्मृतिभ्रंशाद् बुद्धिनाशो बुद्धिनाशात्प्रणश्यति ॥

chains.summary: Desire, anger and greed are the threefold gate that ruins the self. A person gives up these three. Freed from them, that person does what is good for the self and reaches the highest.
chains.title: The three gates

verses.m: Threefold is the gate of hell that destroys the self: desire, anger and greed. Therefore one should give up these three.
verses.sa: त्रिविधं नरकस्येदं द्वारं नाशनमात्मनः । कामः क्रोधस्तथा लोभस्तस्मादेतत्त्रयं त्यजेत् ॥

verses.m: Released from these three gates of darkness, Kaunteya, a person does what is good for the self and so reaches the highest goal.
verses.sa: एतैर्विमुक्तः कौन्तेय तमोद्वारैस्त्रिभिर्नरः । आचरत्यात्मनः श्रेयस्ततो याति परां गतिम् ॥

chains.summary: If you have patience, you do not need armor. If you have anger, you do not need enemies.
chains.title: With patience, who needs armour

verses.m: If you have forbearance, what need of armour? If you have anger, what need of enemies? If you have kinsmen, what need of fire? If a friend, what need of magic medicines? If the wicked are around, what need of snakes? If spotless learning, what need of riches? If modesty, what need of ornaments? If fine poetry, what need of a kingdom?
verses.sa: क्षान्तिश्चेत् कवचेन किं किमरिभिः क्रोधोऽस्ति चेद्देहिनां ज्ञातिश्चेदनलेन किं यदि सुहृद् दिव्यौषधैः किं फलम् । किं सर्पैर्यदि दुर्जनाः किमु धनैर्विद्या न वन्द्या यदि व्रीडा चेत्किमु भूषणैः सुकविता यद्यस्ति राज्येन किम् ॥

depicts.m: An angry person never knows what should be said and what should not. For the angry there is nothing they won't do, and nothing they won't say.
depicts.r: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
depicts.sa: वाच्यावाच्ये हि कुपितो न प्रजानाति कर्हिचित् / नाकार्यमस्ति क्रुद्धस्य नावाच्यं विद्यते तथा
depicts.why: Pictures the angry mind for which nothing is off limits.

gloss: The fire that rises when wanting is blocked (kāmāt krodho 'bhijāyate) and then clouds judgement.

heals.m: One from whom the world does not shrink and who does not shrink from the world, who is free from elation, impatience, fear and agitation, is dear to me.
heals.sa: यस्मान्नोद्विजते लोको लोकान्नोद्विजते च यः । हर्षामर्षभयोद्वेगैर्मुक्तो यः स च मे प्रियः ॥

heals.m: Speech that causes no distress, that is truthful, pleasant and beneficial, and the regular study of sacred texts: this is called austerity of speech.
heals.sa: अनुद्वेगकरं वाक्यं सत्यं प्रियहितं च यत् । स्वाध्यायाभ्यसनं चैव वाङ्मयं तप उच्यते ॥
heals.why: Gives a four part test to run before speaking in heat.

heals.m: One whose mind is not shaken by sorrow, who has no craving for pleasures, and who is free from attachment, fear and anger, is called a sage of steady mind.
heals.why: Shows the steady mind pictured as free of anger.

heals.m: If you have forbearance, what need of armour? If you have anger, what need of enemies? If you have kinsmen, what need of fire? If a friend, what need of magic medicines? If the wicked are around, what need of snakes? If spotless learning, what need of riches? If modesty, what need of ornaments? If fine poetry, what need of a kingdom?
heals.sa: क्षान्तिश्चेत् कवचेन किं किमरिभिः क्रोधोऽस्ति चेद्देहिनां ज्ञातिश्चेदनलेन किं यदि सुहृद् दिव्यौषधैः किं फलम् । किं सर्पैर्यदि दुर्जनाः किमु धनैर्विद्या न वन्द्या यदि व्रीडा चेत्किमु भूषणैः सुकविता यद्यस्ति राज्येन किम् ॥

heals.m: Seeing Parashurama's fire of anger rise with each of Lakshman's replies, which fell on it like offerings of ghee, Ram, sun of the Raghu line, spoke words like water.
heals.sa: लखन उतर आहुति सरिस भृगुबर कोपु कृसानु। बढ़त देखि जल सम बचन बोले रघुकुलभानु ॥
heals.why: Shows anger in a room growing by what is fed to it.

heals.m: Ten people do not know what is right, Dhritarashtra; hear who they are: the drunk, the careless, the deranged, the exhausted, the angry, the starving, the hurried, the greedy, the frightened and the lustful. So a wise person does not let himself be caught in these states.
heals.sa: दश धर्मं न जानन्ति धृतराष्ट्र निबोध तान् / मत्तः प्रमत्त उन्मत्तः श्रान्तः क्रुद्धो बुभुक्षितः त्वरमाणश्च लुब्धश्च भीतः कामी च ते दश / तस्मादेतेषु भावेषु न प्रसञ्जेत पण्डितः
heals.why: Lists anger as a state where right and wrong cannot be seen.

heals.m: Liking and disliking belong to the mind, and you are never the mind. You are awareness itself, free of thought-forms and unchanging. Live happily.
heals.sa: रागद्वेषौ मनोधर्मौ न मनस्ते कदाचन । निर्विकल्पोऽसि बोधात्मा निर्विकारः सुखं चर ॥
heals.why: Names the heat of dislike as seen, not self.

heals.m: It is bondage when the mind wants something, grieves over something, drops or grabs something, is pleased or angered by something. It is freedom when the mind does not want, grieve, drop, grab, delight or rage.
heals.sa: तदा बन्धो यदा चित्तं किञ्चिद् वाञ्छति शोचति । किञ्चिन् मुञ्चति गृण्हाति किञ्चिद् दृष्यति कुप्यति ॥ तदा मुक्तिर्यदा चित्तं न वाञ्छति न शोचति । न मुञ्चति न गृण्हाति न हृष्यति न कुप्यति ॥

hero.m: From anger comes delusion; from delusion, confusion of memory; from confusion of memory, the ruin of understanding; and with understanding ruined, a person is lost.
hero.sa: क्रोधाद्भवति संमोहः संमोहात्स्मृतिविभ्रमः । स्मृतिभ्रंशाद् बुद्धिनाशो बुद्धिनाशात्प्रणश्यति ॥

loci.m: From anger comes delusion; from delusion, confusion of memory; from confusion of memory, the ruin of understanding; and with understanding ruined, a person is lost.
loci.sa: क्रोधाद्भवति संमोहः संमोहात्स्मृतिविभ्रमः । स्मृतिभ्रंशाद् बुद्धिनाशो बुद्धिनाशात्प्रणश्यति ॥

loci.m: The Blessed Lord said: It is desire, it is anger, born of the quality of passion; all-devouring and greatly harmful. Know this to be the enemy here.
loci.sa: श्री भगवानुवाचकाम एष क्रोध एष रजोगुणसमुद्भवः । महाशनो महापाप्मा विद्ध्येनमिह वैरिणम् ॥

loci.m: An angry person never knows what should and should not be said. For the angry, nothing is off limits to do or to say.
loci.sa: वाच्यावाच्यं प्रकुपितो न विजानाति कर्हिचित्। नाकार्यमस्ति क्रुद्धस्य नावाच्यं विद्यते क्वचित्॥

practices.m: Contact of the senses with their objects brings cold and heat, pleasure and pain. They come and go and do not last. Bear them patiently, Arjuna.
When, like a tortoise drawing in its limbs on every side, a person withdraws the senses from their objects, his wisdom is firmly set.
practices.sa: यदा संहरते चायं कूर्मोऽङ्गानीव सर्वशः । इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेभ्यस्तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥
practices.why: Shows wisdom staying set when the senses are gathered.

practices.m: One who is able, here in this life, before leaving the body, to withstand the surge born of desire and anger, is disciplined; he is a happy person.
practices.sa: शक्नोतीहैव यः सोढुं प्राक्शरीरविमोक्षणात् । कामक्रोधोद्भवं वेगं स युक्तः स सुखी नरः ॥
practices.why: Cultivates the capacity to hold steady while the surge passes.

practices.m: Whether a task is good or bad, a wise person should first carefully weigh its outcome. The result of deeds done in great haste burns the heart like a thorn until one's dying day.
practices.sa: गुणवदगुणवद्वा कुर्वता कार्यजातं परिणतिरवधार्या यत्नतः पण्डितेन । अतिरभसकृतानां कर्मणामाविपत्ते- र्भवति हृदयदाही शल्यतुल्यो विपाकः ॥

practices.m: Good company takes dullness from the mind, sprinkles truth into speech, raises one's dignity, removes wrongdoing, clears the heart and spreads one's good name in every direction. Tell me, what does good company not do for a person?
practices.sa: जाड्यं धियो हरति सिञ्चति वाचि सत्यं मानोन्नतिं दिशति पापमपाकरोति । चेतः प्रसादयति दिक्षु तनोति कीर्तिं सत्सङ्गतिः कथय किं न करोति पुंसाम् ॥
practices.why: Shows removal of dullness of mind.

practices.m: The lowest do not begin at all, for fear of obstacles. The middling begin, but stop when obstacles strike. The best, struck by obstacles again and again, do not give up what they have begun.
practices.sa: प्रारभ्यते न खलु विघ्नभयेन नीचैः प्रारभ्य विघ्नविहता विरमन्ति मध्याः ॥ विघ्नैः पुनः पुनरपि प्रतिहन्यमानाः प्रारब्धमुत्तमगुणा न परित्यजन्ति ॥

practices.m: Make a friend slowly, and give one up slowly. A friendship made slowly is one that lasts long.
practices.sa: चिरेण मित्रं बध्नीयाच्चिरेण च कृतं त्यजेत् / चिरेण हि कृतं मित्रं चिरं धारणमर्हति
practices.why: Take time before binding or breaking a bond.

practices.m: One who does not get angry is better than those who do; the patient are better than the impatient; the humane better than the inhuman; the knowing better than the ignorant.
practices.sa: अक्रोधनः क्रुध्यतां वै विशिष्ट / स्तथा तितिक्षुरतितिक्षोर्विशिष्टः / अमानुषान्मानुषो वै विशिष्ट / स्तथाऽज्ञानाज्ज्ञानवान्वै विशिष्टः

stories.l: Desire unmet becomes anger; see it clearly and you can master it.
stories.s: Arjuna asks why we do wrong as if forced. Krishna names desire, which turns into anger, as the enemy that clouds wisdom like smoke over fire, and tells him to master it.

stories.l: You can try your best for peace and still fail. Others' choices are not your guilt.
stories.s: Returning home after the war, Krishna meets the sage Uttanka, who is furious that Krishna let the cousins destroy each other and threatens to curse him. Krishna explains that he tried hard for peace and was refused, and calms him.

stories.l: Think before you act on an assumption; haste turns misunderstandings into wars.
stories.s: Forest dwellers report that Bharat is coming with an army. Lakshman, sure it is an attack, climbs a tree and swears to destroy him. A voice from the sky warns against acting in haste, and Ram explains that Bharat could never turn against him; power could not corrupt him.
stories.t: Lakshman assumes the worst about Bharat

stories.l: Clever replies feed anger; calm, humble words put it out.
stories.s: Parashurama storms into the wedding hall furious that Shiva's bow is broken. Lakshman answers every threat with a joke, and each reply feeds the fire. Ram steps in with soft words, takes the blame on himself, and calmly points out that an old bow broke at a touch; the sage's anger finally turns to recognition.
stories.t: Parashurama's rage, Lakshman's taunts, Ram's calm
